_note: Public places to learn about each nation's culture. Links out only. Nation-run places first; operator always labeled. No sacred, ceremonial or burial sites. Researched 2026-11-09 for ND, SD, NE, MT, WY.

places.name: MHA Interpretive Center
places.about: The MHA Nation's own center west of New Town, with permanent exhibits and living history programs on Mandan, Hidatsa and Arikara history and culture.
places.notes: Address 3881 Lake Sakakawea Rd, New Town; (701) 627-2238. The center's site lists no hours. ND Tourism lists it as open year-round. Guided tours are booked in advance on the center's site. Coordinates come from the ND Tourism listing (state tourism data), not the center itself. Opened May 2021.

places.name: Knife River Indian Villages National Historic Site
places.about: Remains of Hidatsa earthlodge villages along the Knife River, with a visitor center, a full-size reconstructed earthlodge and walking trails.

sources.name: NPS – Knife River Indian Villages NHS

places.notes: The visitor center and earthlodge are open year-round, 9–5 Central, and closed Thanksgiving, Christmas and New Year's Day. Grounds are open sunrise to sunset. Coordinates are from Wikipedia.

places.name: On-A-Slant Village at Fort Abraham Lincoln State Park
places.operator_name: North Dakota Parks and Recreation Department
places.about: A former Mandan village site near the Heart and Missouri rivers, with reconstructed earthlodges and summer tours that introduce Mandan life.

sources.name: ND Parks and Recreation – Fort Abraham Lincoln State Park
NPS – On-A-Slant Village (Lewis and Clark NHT)

places.notes: Village tours run Memorial Day weekend through Labor Day and need an Interpretive Tour Pass ($8 adult, $5 K-12). The two sources disagree on the earthlodge count: ND Parks says six including a Council Lodge, NPS says five. The ND Parks page gives two different visitor center schedules. Coordinates are Wikipedia's point for the park, not the village itself. The park also covers the Custer-era fort, so the Mandan content is one part of the visit.

places.name: Double Ditch Indian Village State Historic Site
places.operator_name: State Historical Society of North Dakota
places.about: Site of a large Mandan earthlodge village occupied for nearly 300 years, with walking paths and interpretive signs above the Missouri River.
places.notes: Open year-round with free admission. It is an outdoor site with no facilities, on ND 1804 about 7.5 miles north of Bismarck. Coordinates are from Wikipedia. Do not use the SHSND map-link coordinates: they are a generic default that SHSND also uses for Fort Totten. This is an archaeological village site, so MHA Nation should confirm it is comfortable with the listing.

places.name: Fort Totten State Historic Site
places.operator_name: State Historical Society of North Dakota
places.about: An 1867 military post on the Spirit Lake Reservation that later served as an Indian boarding school; original brick buildings now hold exhibits.

sources.name: SHSND – Fort Totten State Historic Site
Wikipedia – Fort Totten State Historic Site

places.notes: Open daily 9–5 from Memorial Day weekend through Labor Day, and by appointment the rest of the year. Grounds are open weekdays year-round. The BIA ran it as a boarding school from 1891 and as a tuberculosis preventorium for Dakota children from 1935 to 1939. The site is state-run, not run by the nation. The page does not detail how much of the exhibit content is Dakota or Spirit Lake history.

places.name: Sitting Bull Visitor Center
places.about: A visitor and cultural center on the Sitting Bull College campus, a starting point for learning Standing Rock history and finding places to visit.
places.notes: The college page says 'Open upon request.' The 2023 guide gave weekday hours of 8:00–4:30. Campus address: 9299 Hwy 24, Fort Yates. Contact Glen Bahm, (701) 854-8088. Coordinates are Wikipedia's point for the college campus, not the building. The guide names the site 'Sitting Bull Visitor Center & Medicine Wheel Park' and also covers Sitting Bull's burial sites. Leave out any directions to burial sites, and don't promote the medicine wheel until the nation confirms.

places.name: Turtle Mountain Chippewa Heritage Center
places.about: Artwork, sculpture and artifacts telling the story of the Chippewa, Cree and Michif people of the Turtle Mountains, plus language classes and local art.

sources.name: ND Tourism – Turtle Mountain Chippewa Heritage Center

places.notes: Address 3959 Sky Dancer Way, Belcourt. Director Danielle Wilkie (2025). Displays were being reworked in 2025. ND Tourism lists it as open year-round, with no hours given. The only web presence found is Facebook. Map listings name a 'Turtle Mountain Chippewa Historical Society', so confirm the operator before publishing.

places.name: Lakota Cultural Center (H.V. Johnston Cultural Center)
places.about: The tribe's cultural center at its Eagle Butte headquarters, with a hall of murals by local artists, Lakota art and crafts, and cultural events.

sources.name: Cheyenne River Sioux Tribe – Cultural Center
Travel South Dakota – Lakota Cultural Center & Gift Shop

places.notes: Address 24352 US Hwy 212, Eagle Butte; (605) 964-2542. Travel South Dakota lists weekday hours of 8–5; the tribe's page gives none. Neither source mentions a museum or permanent artifact exhibits: it is murals, events and a gift shop. The center's own site (crstlakotaculturalcenter.com) blocked automated reading. Built 1973.

places.name: Aktá Lakota Museum & Cultural Center
places.about: A free museum on the St. Joseph's Indian School campus presenting the art, history and culture of Lakota, Dakota and Nakota people.

sources.name: Travel South Dakota Native Tourism fact sheet (Aug 2025)

places.notes: Hours May–Oct: Mon–Sat 8–6, Sun 9–5. Nov–Apr: weekdays 8–4:30. Admission is free. Address 1301 N. Main St. Coordinates are from Wikipedia. The museum is not run by any nation and covers Lakota, Dakota and Nakota peoples broadly, not Crow Creek or Lower Brule in particular. I tagged those two only because they are the nearest nations (needs an editorial decision, see Flags). It is run by a Catholic boarding school, so label the operator plainly.

places.name: Čhatkú Arts Center (formerly The Heritage Center at Maȟpíya Lúta)
places.operator_name: Maȟpíya Lúta (Red Cloud Indian School, Inc.)
places.about: An arts center on the Maȟpíya Lúta campus holding about 13,000 works of historic and contemporary Lakota and Native art, home of the Red Cloud Indian Art Show.

sources.name: ICT – Čhatkú Arts Center carries a legacy forward

places.notes: New name and building as of 2026. ICT says it moved into the new facility on June 6, 2026, and its homepage says 'open'. Address 100 Mission Drive, Pine Ridge. ICT gives summer hours of Mon–Sat 10–5 and Sun 1–5. Travel SD gives weekdays 10–5. Its own 'Hours & Directions' page was not read. Admission is free. Coordinates are Wikipedia's point for the school campus. Visits can be booked through FareHarbor from mahpiyaluta.org.

places.name: Oglala Lakota College Historical Center
places.about: Photographs, artwork and an audio narration trace Oglala Lakota history from the early 1800s through 1890, with Oglala Lakota artists featured each summer.
places.notes: Free admission, Mon–Fri 9–5. It is 8 miles southeast of Sharps Corner, or 7 miles southwest of Kyle. Wikipedia's coordinates are for the main campus, not this building, so lat/lon are left null. The second source was found in search but not opened.

places.name: Sicangu Heritage Center
places.about: Museum and archives at Sinte Gleska University, with a permanent exhibit on Lakota kinship and the tiyóšpaye way of life, plus beadwork.

sources.name: Travel South Dakota – Rosebud Sioux Tribe

places.notes: It sits on the SGU campus at Antelope Lake, just east of Mission. It is the official archive of the Rosebud Sioux Tribe. The university's page lists no hours or public access. News coverage says to contact the center to arrange a visit. Curator/director Keli Brings Three White Horses, 605-856-8211.

places.name: Ponca Tribal Museum
places.about: The tribe's museum holds one of Chief Standing Bear's headdresses, repatriated headdresses, beadwork, tools, instruments and photos of the 1877 delegation.

sources.name: Ponca Tribe of Nebraska – Tribal Museum
NPS – Ponca Tribal Museum (Lewis and Clark NHT)

places.notes: Mon–Fri 8–4. Address 88915 521 Ave, Niobrara; 402-857-3519. It shares a building with the tribal library and archives. Visit Nebraska also lists a Ponca Educational Trail and Earthlodge nearby, next to the powwow grounds. That could be a separate entry if the tribe confirms it.

places.name: Angel DeCora Museum & Research Center
places.about: The tribe's free museum and research center sharing Winnebago (Ho-Chunk) history, art and culture through artifacts such as hand-loomed bags and historic papers.

sources.name: Winnebago Tribe of Nebraska – Angel DeCora Museum
Visit Nebraska – Angel De Cora Museum and Research Center

places.notes: Address 415 E. Littlepriest Dr.; open 8:00–4:30, free. The tribe's page gives no days of the week. Spelling: the tribe writes 'DeCora', while Visit Nebraska writes 'De Cora'; use the tribe's form. The 'Ho-Chunk' wording in the about line is mine. Check that the nation is comfortable with it, or use 'Winnebago'. The Visit Nebraska page was found in search but not opened.

places.name: Dr. Susan La Flesche Picotte Center
places.operator_name: Dr. Susan La Flesche Picotte Center
places.about: The restored hospital built by Dr. Susan La Flesche Picotte, now holding a memorial museum and exhibits of Omaha Tribe art, artifacts and history.

sources.name: Dr. Susan La Flesche Picotte Center
Visit Nebraska – Dr. Susan LaFlesche Picotte Center

places.notes: Reopened after restoration June 22, 2025. Hours May–Oct: Tue–Sat 10–3:30. Winter: Wed–Sat 10–3. Large groups call ahead. Address 503 Matthewson St; 531-254-0625. It is a National Historic Landmark on the Omaha Reservation. The operator's legal form and its formal tie to the Omaha Tribe are not stated.

places.name: Three Chiefs Culture Center
places.about: The Salish, Pend d'Oreille and Kootenai cultural center shows museum exhibits, collections that survived the 2020 fire, cultural demonstrations and Native-made art.
places.notes: This is the former People's Center. It was damaged by arson in 2020, renamed, and moved to St. Ignatius and then back to a temporary building in Pablo. threechiefs.org gives the address as 36042 Major Houle Rd, but cskt.org lists 42487 Complex Blvd, which may be the tribal complex. Weekday hours appear on the site twice and conflict, and summer Saturday hours are listed. Closed Sundays and on tribal holidays.

places.name: CSKT Bison Range
places.operator_name: Confederated Salish and Kootenai Tribes (Natural Resource Department)
places.about: Congress restored this bison range to the Tribes in 2020. Visitors find a tribally run visitor center and scenic drives through bison country.
places.notes: The visitor center is open daily 8am to 5pm. Prairie Drive is open all year, weather permitting. Red Sleep Drive is open May to October only. The coordinates come from Wikipedia and mark the range headquarters at Moiese. The official mailing town is Charlo.

places.name: Museum of the Plains Indian
places.operator_name: U.S. Department of the Interior, Indian Arts and Crafts Board
places.about: Founded in 1941 on the Blackfeet Reservation, the museum shows Northern Plains clothing, horse gear and art, plus rotating shows of Native artists.

sources.name: IACB: Museum of the Plains Indian Location and Hours
NPS: Museum of the Plains Indian

places.notes: The museum is open. The IACB lists a 2026 Summer Showcase (June 26 to Sept 30, 2026) and an America 250 exhibition (July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027), and posts no closure notice. Address: 19 Museum Loop. October to May it is open Tuesday to Friday, 10am to 4pm. June to September it is open Tuesday to Friday, 9am to 4:45pm. Photography is not allowed inside. The museum is federally run, not run by the nation, and its collection covers several Northern Plains nations.

places.name: St. Mary Visitor Center, Glacier National Park
places.about: Permanent exhibits made with Blackfeet, Salish, Pend d'Oreille and Kootenai advisors share tribal views of the land, place names and elders' oral histories.

sources.name: NPS news release: New Exhibits Tell Native American Story of Glacier (2010)
NPS: American Indian Tribes of Glacier

places.notes: The exhibit, At Home In This Place, was installed in 2010 according to an archived release. The current NPS page lists exhibits but does not name them, so it is worth confirming the exhibit is still installed. The center is staffed in summer only. Glacier's Native America Speaks talks are a program, not a place.

places.name: Chief Plenty Coups (Alek-Chea-Ahoosh) State Park
places.about: On the Crow Reservation, this National Historic Landmark keeps Chief Plenty Coups' log home and farmstead, with a visitor center and creekside trail.

sources.name: Montana FWP: Chief Plenty Coups State Park
Wikipedia: Chief Plenty Coups State Park and Home

places.notes: The park is day use only. The visitor center and the Chief's house are open 10am to 5pm. Summer park hours are daily; in winter the park is open Wednesday to Sunday. FWP says the park includes a sacred spring. Copy should not describe the spring or direct visitors to it.

places.name: Little Bighorn Battlefield National Monument
places.about: The battlefield's Indian Memorial, themed Peace Through Unity, honors the Crow, Cheyenne, Arapaho, Lakota and Arikara people who fought here in 1876.
places.notes: A new visitor center is under construction. NPS hopes to finish it by the end of 2026, with exhibits installed before summer 2027. Until then a temporary contact station is open. Parking is limited, and part of the lot is closed from Nov 25 until the work is done. The coordinates come from Wikipedia. The NPS Indian Memorial page names the Cheyenne and Arapaho, not specifically the Northern bands; the directory's link to the Northern Cheyenne and Northern Arapaho is my inference.

places.name: Rosebud Battlefield State Park
places.about: The 1876 battlefield the Northern Cheyenne call Where the Girl Saved Her Brother, with interpretive displays and mowed paths across open prairie.

sources.name: Montana FWP: Rosebud Battlefield State Park
Montana State Parks Foundation: Rosebud Battlefield

places.notes: The park is open all year, day use only. The road in crosses private property. Interpretation is limited to brochures and a display. FWP also names Crow and Shoshone scouts who rode with Crook. I tagged only the Northern Cheyenne because the content is mainly about them. The site also includes a buffalo jump with petroglyphs. Copy should not encourage visitors to approach rock art.

places.name: Plains Indian Museum, Buffalo Bill Center of the West
places.operator_name: Buffalo Bill Center of the West
places.about: A museum of Plains peoples' art and daily life. Its Land of Many Gifts gallery is built around an Apsáalooke (Crow) lodge.

sources.name: Buffalo Bill Center of the West: Plan your visit
Points West: Launching the Plains Indian Museum

places.notes: This museum covers Plains peoples generally. Its galleries also feature Oglala Lakota, Cheyenne (Tsistsistas) and Mandan material, and the museum's history includes Eastern Shoshone and Northern Arapaho objects and advisors. I tagged only the Crow, where the gallery content is specific. From December to February it is open Thursday to Sunday only. The coordinates come from Wikipedia and mark the Center campus. The address is 720 Sheridan Ave.

places.name: Eastern Shoshone Tribal Cultural Center
places.about: The Tribe's cultural center shares Shoshone history through artifacts, artwork, photographs, maps and treaties, along with language-learning resources.

sources.name: Travel Wyoming: Eastern Shoshone Tribal Cultural Center
Wyoming Public Media, Dec 2025: Eastern Shoshone Cultural Hub project

places.notes: The Tribe's page lists the address (#14 North Fork Road) and phone numbers ((307) 332-3532 or 332-3055) but no hours and no description of the exhibits. Travel Wyoming lists hours of Monday to Friday, 8am to 4:45pm. Wyoming Public Media reported in Dec 2025 that the center and museum are in the Fort Washakie School. A new Eastern Shoshone Cultural Hub (easternshoshonemuseum.com) is planned but not built. The 'about' line relies on Travel Wyoming for exhibit content. I used the Tribe's page for address, phone and language resources.

places.name: Northern Arapaho Experience Room
places.operator_name: Wind River Hotel & Casino (owned by the Northern Arapaho Tribe)
places.about: A room of Northern Arapaho artifacts, paintings, photographs and video, with elder-led language and storytelling sessions and weekly summer dance exhibitions.

sources.name: Wind River Hotel & Casino: Northern Arapaho Experience Room
Travel Wyoming: Northern Arapaho Experience Culture Room

places.notes: The room is off the lobby of the tribally owned hotel and casino at 180 Red Wolf Place. It is open daily 9am to 1pm and 2pm to 6pm, phone (307) 856-3964. Travel Wyoming says to call ahead to arrange elder sessions. It is a cultural exhibit space, not a casino listing, but the Library may want to decide how to present a venue inside a casino.

places.name: Fort Union Trading Post National Historic Site
places.about: This reconstructed fur-trade post was built with Assiniboine permission. The Assiniboine were its main trading partners, and their story runs through the site.

sources.name: NPS: Fort Union Trading Post NHS
Wikipedia: Fort Union Trading Post NHS

places.notes: It is about 25 miles from Williston on the ND/MT line, and it is the closest place on this list to Medora. NPS links the Assiniboine to both Fort Peck and Fort Belknap today. It is a fur-trade site, not run with the nations, so its fit as a place to learn about these nations needs an editorial call. I did not verify hours or season.

places.name: North Dakota Heritage Center & State Museum
places.operator_name: State Historical Society of North Dakota
places.about: The state museum on the Capitol grounds. Its Early Peoples gallery is devoted to the Native peoples of North Dakota, and it holds the Native American Hall of Honor.

sources.name: North Dakota Heritage Center & State Museum

places.notes: Regional museum covering several nations, so nations is empty on purpose; it shows only through the nearby rule (75 miles). Gallery names are from the museum's own home page. Coordinates from Wikipedia. Admission not confirmed.

places.name: South Dakota Cultural Heritage Center
places.about: The state history museum north of the Capitol. Its Oyate Tawicoh'an gallery, The Ways of the People, covers Dakota, Nakota and Lakota history and beliefs.

sources.name: South Dakota State Historical Society Museum

places.notes: Regional museum covering several nations, so nations is empty on purpose; it shows only through the nearby rule (75 miles). Reopened July 1, 2026 after a three-year renovation; confirm the gallery name is unchanged after the renovation. Coordinates from Wikipedia (South Dakota State Historical Society article). 900 Governors Drive; (605) 773-3458.

places.name: Alaska Native Heritage Center
places.about: Statewide gathering place in Anchorage sharing the traditions, languages and arts of Alaska Native cultures through exhibits, films, live programs and dance performances.
places.notes: 8800 Heritage Center Drive, Anchorage, AK 99504; (907) 330-8000. Seasonal: fuller summer program (guided tours, dance, Native Games) and a self-guided weekday winter schedule. Covers all of Alaska's Native peoples, so no single nation tagged; serves Anchorage-area nations (Eklutna, Knik and others) via the nearby rule. Coordinates from OpenStreetMap (Nominatim) museum node.

places.name: Anchorage Museum – Smithsonian Arctic Studies Center gallery
places.operator_name: Anchorage Museum, with the Smithsonian Arctic Studies Center
places.about: Living Our Cultures, Sharing Our Heritage: more than 600 Alaska Native objects on long-term Smithsonian loan, with videos, oral histories and recordings of Alaska Native storytellers.
places.notes: 625 C Street, Anchorage, AK 99501; (907) 929-9200. Exhibit covers peoples statewide, so nations []. Coordinates from OpenStreetMap (Nominatim) museum node. Operator type: Anchorage Museum is a nonprofit/municipal partnership; confirm label if Matt wants it as 'other'.

places.name: Sealaska Heritage Institute – Walter Soboleff Building
places.about: Sealaska Heritage Institute's downtown Juneau building, with a clan house, exhibit galleries and monumental Northwest Coast art sharing Tlingit, Haida and Tsimshian culture.
places.notes: Front and Seward Streets area, downtown Juneau (OSM gives 105 Heritage Way); (907) 463-4844. SHI's page wording on open days is ambiguous; confirm. Covers Tlingit, Haida and Tsimshian peoples of Southeast Alaska, so nations []; Juneau-based Central Council of the Tlingit & Haida Indian Tribes and Douglas Indian Association get it via the nearby rule. Did not check the separate Sealaska Heritage Arts Campus. Coordinates from OpenStreetMap (Nominatim) building.

places.name: Iñupiat Heritage Center
places.about: North Slope Borough center in Utqiaġvik that promotes Iñupiat history, language and culture, with exhibits, collections, a library and traditional craft demonstrations.

sources.name: North Slope Borough – Iñupiat Heritage Center
NPS – Alaska Native Heritage and the Iñupiat Heritage Center

places.notes: NPS lists 5421 North Star St; OSM node shows 541 North Star St; confirm. Center phone (907) 852-0422. NPS says open year-round (page last updated 2021). Affiliated area of New Bedford Whaling NHP. Serves the North Slope whaling villages generally, so nations []; Native Village of Barrow and Iñupiat Community of the Arctic Slope (both Utqiaġvik) come in via the nearby rule. Coordinates from OpenStreetMap (Nominatim) museum node.

places.name: Simon Paneak Memorial Museum
places.operator_name: North Slope Borough, Iñupiat History, Language & Culture Department
places.about: Small community museum in Anaktuvuk Pass on the Nunamiut, the inland Iñupiat of the central Brooks Range: their history, caribou hunting, seasonal life and the village's founding.

sources.name: North Slope Borough – Simon Paneak Memorial Museum

places.notes: P.O. Box 21085, Anaktuvuk Pass, AK 99721; (907) 661-3413. Reached only by air (flights from Fairbanks); short walk from the airstrip. Established 1986 by the community. Tagged to Village of Anaktuvuk Pass because the museum is about the Nunamiut of that village. Coordinates from OpenStreetMap (Nominatim) museum node (matches Wikipedia 68.14412, -151.73656).

places.name: Yupiit Piciryarait Museum
places.about: Museum inside Bethel's Yupiit Piciryarait Cultural Center showing Yup'ik, Cup'ik and Dene objects of the Yukon-Kuskokwim Delta, including clothing, tools, masks and a full-size skin boat.
places.notes: 401 Chief Eddie Hoffman Highway, Bethel (AVCP page also spells it 'Homan'); (907) 543-8541; Museum@avcp.org. Reopened April 2025 after a long closure; weekday afternoon hours per KYUK; AVCP says access also available on request. AVCP is the regional tribal consortium for 56 Delta tribes, so nations []; Delta villages within 75 miles get it via the nearby rule. Coordinates are OSM for the adjacent UAF Kuskokwim Campus, which owns the cultural center building; no OSM node for the museum itself, so confirm.

places.name: Alutiiq Museum and Archaeological Repository
places.about: Kodiak museum sharing 7,800 years of Alutiiq/Sugpiaq heritage through ancestral objects, local history and living traditions, plus changing exhibits.
places.notes: 215 Mission Road, Kodiak, AK 99615; 844-425-8844. Founded and sustained by Kodiak Native organizations (KANA, Koniag and village corporations). Operator name 'Alutiiq Heritage Foundation' is from general knowledge, not the visit page; confirm. Covers the Kodiak archipelago's Alutiiq tribes, so nations []; Sun'aq, Afognak, Tangirnaq, Ouzinkie, Port Lions and Old Harbor fall within range via the nearby rule. Coordinates are OSM for the 215 Mission Road address (OSM returned two points; used the first).

places.name: Morris Thompson Cultural and Visitors Center
places.operator_name: Morris Thompson Cultural and Visitors Center partners (incl. Denakkanaaga, Alaska Geographic, Alaska Public Lands Information Center)
places.about: Free center on the Chena River in Fairbanks on Dena lands, with dioramas, art, clothing and tools of Interior Alaska peoples and cultural programs and demonstrations.

sources.name: Morris Thompson Cultural and Visitors Center

places.notes: 101 Dunkel Street, Fairbanks, AK 99701; 907-459-3700. Open year-round. The site does not name a single operator; partner list from the homepage. Interior Alaska Athabascan focus but not one nation, so nations []. Coordinates from OpenStreetMap (Nominatim) building.

places.name: University of Alaska Museum of the North
places.about: University museum in Fairbanks where the Rose Berry Alaska Art Gallery shows ancient ivory carvings and Alaska Native objects, and the Gallery of Alaska covers each region's people.
places.notes: 1962 Yukon Drive, Fairbanks, AK 99775; (907) 474-7505. Visit page blocked automated reading, so open status not confirmed from the visit page; the 2026 gallery guide implies it is operating. Statewide scope, nations []. Coordinates from OpenStreetMap (Nominatim) museum node.

places.name: Sitka National Historical Park
places.about: Sitka park with Tlingit and Haida totem poles on a coastal trail, the site of a battle between Russian traders and the Kiks.ádi Tlingit, and the Russian Bishop's House.
places.notes: Visitor center at 106 Metlakatla Street, Sitka (OSM); mailing 103 Monastery St. NPS hours page gave no current visitor-center hours; confirm season. Interprets Kiks.ádi Tlingit history; left nations [] pending Matt's call on tagging Sitka Tribe of Alaska (see questions). Coordinates from OpenStreetMap (Nominatim) ranger station at 106 Metlakatla St.

places.name: Xunaa Shuká Hít (Huna Tribal House)
places.operator_name: National Park Service, with the Hoonah Indian Association
places.about: Clan house at Bartlett Cove in Glacier Bay National Park honoring the Huna Lingít clans' homeland, with carved house posts, totem poles and summer talks by tribal interpreters.
places.notes: On the Lingít Trail about a quarter mile from Glacier Bay Lodge, Bartlett Cove. Exterior open year-round per NPS; 2026 schedule shows a summer open house with a tribal interpreter (late May to late August, Tue–Sat afternoons). Joint project of NPS and Hoonah Indian Association; tagged to Hoonah Indian Association. Coordinates from OpenStreetMap (Nominatim) (Xunaa Shuka Hit node, Tlingit Trail).

places.name: Ilanka Cultural Center
places.about: The Native Village of Eyak's museum in Cordova, with tribal objects from Prince William Sound and the Copper River Delta and an orca skeleton hanging in the lobby.

sources.name: Native Village of Eyak – Cultural Department

places.notes: Tribe's page gives both 711 First Street and 110 Nicholoff Way (same building as tribal offices); confirm. (907) 424-7903; culture@eyak-nsn.gov. Old domain ilankacenter.org now hosts an unrelated site; do not link it. Coordinates are OSM for 711 1st Street, Cordova.

places.name: K'Beq' Cultural Site
places.about: Kenaitze Indian Tribe's summer site on the Kenai River, with a boardwalk around an ancient Dena'ina house site, interpretive signs, a historic cabin and walks led by tribal members.

sources.name: Kenaitze Indian Tribe – K'Beq' Cultural Site

places.notes: Mile 52.6 Sterling Highway, across from the Russian River Campground entrance; 907-395-7985. Seasonal (June–September); the tribe's page still shows 2024 season details, so confirm the 2026/2027 season. On Chugach National Forest land. Coordinates from OpenStreetMap (Nominatim) (K'Beq Footprints Heritage Site).

places.name: Museum of the Aleutians
places.about: Unalaska museum and archaeological repository sharing the cultural legacy of the Aleutian Islands, including Unangax̂ art, history and traditional boats, plus Russian-era and WWII history.
places.notes: 314 Salmon Way, Unalaska, AK; 907-581-5150. Summer and winter schedules differ; extra openings for ship visits. Regional Unangax̂ scope, nations []; Qawalangin Tribe of Unalaska is within range via the nearby rule. Coordinates from OpenStreetMap (Nominatim) museum node.

places.name: Northwest Arctic Heritage Center
places.operator_name: National Park Service (Western Arctic National Parklands)
places.about: Free National Park Service museum in Kotzebue on Arctic wildlife, geology, and Iñupiaq culture and subsistence, with films, books and park trip-planning help.
places.notes: 171 Third Ave, Kotzebue, AK 99752; (907) 318-2230. Open weekdays year-round, closed federal holidays. Northwest Arctic Iñupiaq region generally, nations []; Native Village of Kotzebue and nearby villages get it via the nearby rule. Coordinates are OSM (node tagged on 2nd Avenue; NPS gives 171 Third Ave), close enough for the map but confirm.

places.name: Carrie M. McLain Memorial Museum
places.about: Nome's free city museum in the Richard Foster Building, with exhibits on Bering Strait history including Inupiat culture and an Inupiat boat.

sources.name: City of Nome – Carrie M. McLain Memorial Museum

places.notes: Richard Foster Building, 100 W 7th Avenue, Nome; 907-443-6630. City page lists Mon–Sat afternoon hours. Operator not named on the page; assumed City of Nome because the page is on the city's site. The URL is the city's CivicPlus host; swap in the nomealaska.org address if the city has one. Coordinates are OSM for 100 W 7th Ave (Kegoayah Kozga Library, same building). Covers the Bering Strait region generally; Nome Eskimo Community, King Island, Solomon and Council (Nome HQs) get it via the nearby rule.

places.name: Agua Caliente Cultural Museum
places.operator_name: Agua Caliente Band of Cahuilla Indians
places.about: The Agua Caliente Band's museum at its downtown Palm Springs cultural plaza, with exhibits on Agua Caliente Cahuilla history, a changing gallery and a native plant garden.

sources.name: Visit Greater Palm Springs – Agua Caliente Cultural Plaza

places.notes: Opened Nov 2023 in the Agua Caliente Cultural Plaza (with the Spa at Séc-he). Both accmuseum.org and aguacaliente.org sit behind Cloudflare and blocked full page reads; the museum's own site confirmed name and mission but not address or hours. Address 140 N Indian Canyon Dr, Palm Springs is from press coverage, not the museum's site — confirm. Coordinates from OpenStreetMap (Nominatim) geocode of that address.

places.name: Barona Cultural Center & Museum
places.about: San Diego County's first museum on an Indian reservation, presenting Kumeyaay culture through collections, changing exhibits, a native plant garden and a research library.

sources.name: Barona Band of Mission Indians – History

places.notes: 1095 Barona Road, Lakeside, CA 92040; 619-443-7003 x219. Museum site says admission is free and the research library is by appointment. Barona is not in nations_california.json (it shares the Capitan Grande reservation with Viejas), so nations is [] — see questions.
